newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower, Amin Shah's stocks gain.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower, Amin Shah's stocks gain.

text.p: Blue chips led the market's broad fall in thin, uninspired trading as investors' locked in gains after Tuesday's surge, dealers said.

"After the window dressing, you would expect the market to come off," said Leong Yoon Siang at TA Securities' international division. Other traders said knee-jerk reaction to the Dow's 101-point drop on Tuesday and the closure of Singapore and Japanese markets dampened activity in Kuala Lumpur.
The Composite Index fell 7.43 points to 1,230.53.
The only excitement was provided by the surge of stocks linked to Malay businessman Amin Shah Omar Shah.
"Apart from Amin Shah and selected second board counters, the market is dead," said a local institutional dealer.
Shares of shipbuilder PSC Industries jumped 6.95 ringgit or 28.6 percent to 31.25, before being suspended in the afternoon pending a news announcement.
Other Amin Shah counters also surged, but were not suspended. Khong Guan rose 1.90 ringgit to 14.70, Setron up 70 cents to 5.85 and Actacorp firmed 45 cents to 8.50.
Amin Shah and other officials at his holding company, Business Focus, could not be immediately reached for comment.
